source_title: Luceco plc Annual Report and Financial Statements 2019
availability_evidence: The issuer-hosted annual report states on pages 55, 94, 105 and 146 that the Strategic Report and financial statements were approved or authorised for issue on 23 April 2020; the PDF is preserved with its hash in the source index.
observation: Luceco entered the pandemic from a materially improved 2019 position: revenue rose 5% to £172.1m, adjusted operating margin doubled to 10.5%, free cash flow rose to £18.9m and leverage halved to 1.06x. By April 2020, however, lockdowns had reduced revenue to about 50% of normal, prompting furlough, reduced Chinese production headcount, pay cuts and discretionary-spend cancellation; monthly cash outflow was limited to £0.5m and covenant resets were agreed for a severe downside case, with £24.5m of undrawn facilities.
already_announced_exclusion: The pandemic furlough, Chinese headcount reduction, temporary pay cuts, dividend suspension, discretionary-spend cancellation and prior closure of loss-making US operations were already announced or undertaken before cutoff and are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Acute pandemic revenue, workforce and covenant pressure is explicit, but the actions were already public and the improved pre-pandemic margin, low leverage, adequate liquidity and limited cash burn provide substantial contrary evidence.

source_title: Luceco plc Annual Report and Financial Statements 2021
availability_evidence: The issuer-hosted annual report states on pages 57, 105, 116 and 156 that the Strategic Report and financial statements were approved or authorised for issue on 22 March 2022; the PDF is preserved with its hash in the source index.
observation: Supply-chain disruption and £13.6m of input-cost and currency headwinds pressured gross margin and free-cash-flow conversion. Luceco nevertheless increased revenue 29.5% to £228.2m, adjusted operating profit 30% to £39.0m and adjusted operating margin to 17.1%; free-cash-flow margin fell to 8.2% and cash conversion to 89.7%, but covenant leverage remained low at 0.7x. France was consolidated into Southern Europe and the loss-making Northern European operation was scheduled to close, generating £2.3m of restructuring cost and £0.8m annual savings.
already_announced_exclusion: The France consolidation and announced closure of the Germany/Northern Europe operation, including the associated restructuring charge, were already public before cutoff and are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Inflation, supply-chain pressure and weaker cash conversion are credible but contained; strong revenue and profit growth, stable operating margin, low leverage and completed or announced European actions provide dominant contrary evidence.

source_title: Luceco plc Annual Report and Financial Statements 2023
availability_evidence: The issuer-hosted annual report states on pages 76, 116, 128 and 171 that the Strategic Report and financial statements were approved or authorised for issue on 25 March 2024; the PDF is preserved with its hash in the source index.
observation: Post-pandemic destocking, a 5.8% decline in addressable-market output, foreign-exchange and wage headwinds created pressure, but like-for-like revenue grew 1.7%, adjusted operating profit rose to £24.0m and adjusted operating margin improved 80bps to 11.5%. Free cash flow fell to £18.0m from £30.7m yet remained positive, covenant leverage improved to 0.6x and net debt was £18.4m. The prior Germany and France closures generated no new restructuring cost in 2023.
already_announced_exclusion: The Germany and France closures and related prior-year restructuring entries were completed and already public before cutoff; acquisition integration, facility investment and ordinary efficiency actions are excluded from the target definition.
review_note: Weak markets and lower free cash flow create moderate pressure, while market outperformance, margin and profit improvement, continuing cash generation and low leverage provide strong quantified offsets.
